primaries.name: tsp_local_search
primaries.discriminator: Instruction asks for a single Hamiltonian cycle visiting all cities exactly once and returning to start, with only coordinates given (no capacity/vehicles).
primaries.algorithm_skeleton: Precompute pairwise distance matrix → nearest-neighbor (multi-start) constructive seed → 2-opt / Or-opt local search using O(1) delta evaluation → optionally randomized restarts; output permutation tour.
core_constraints: Tour visits every city exactly once and returns to the start (Hamiltonian cycle).
Output schema must match evaluator: if benchmark is multi-instance, enumerate every instance and emit one tour per instance.
Distance computation must be consistent between solver and evaluator (same metric, same rounding).

primaries.name: cvrp_cluster_then_route
primaries.discriminator: Instruction specifies a depot, a fleet of K vehicles with capacity, customer demands/locations, and asks for per-vehicle routes (possibly with workload balance / spatial compactness / extra side constraints).
primaries.algorithm_skeleton: Partition customers (K-means on coordinates, optionally weighted by demand and constrained by per-cluster capacity) → assign each cluster to a vehicle → solve per-cluster TSP via NN + 2-opt/Or-opt with delta evaluation → rebalance boundary customers to the nearest feasible cluster when capacity/side-constraints are violated → compute travel time using the specified speed model and service times.
core_constraints: Per-vehicle load must not exceed capacity.
Each customer is served exactly once by exactly one vehicle; route starts and ends at the depot.
Number of routes must not exceed available vehicles.
All edges/moves must be checked against any case-specific feasibility rules (segregation, restrictions) before being accepted, not only at final validation.
Travel time/cost must be computed with the speed/service-time model the instruction specifies, consistently across construction and local search.

extension_recipes.large_n_scaling: Precompute full O(n^2) distance matrix as a numpy array of float32; use multi-start nearest-neighbor (e.g., 10-20 different seed cities); run 2-opt with O(1) delta cost (compare d[i-1,i]+d[j,j+1] vs d[i-1,j]+d[i,j+1]); for n≈1000 use neighbor-list pruning (only consider j among k-nearest of i, k≈20) to keep sweeps fast; finish with Or-opt pass.
extension_recipes.multi_instance_io: At entry, enumerate the dataset directory or group input rows by instance_id; assert count equals the spec (e.g., 128); loop over each instance with a fixed per-instance time budget; collect tours into a single solution.json keyed by instance_id matching evaluator schema; never hardcode a single input file.
extension_recipes.dual_speed_travel_time: Implement travel_time(u,v) that uses 70 km/h when exactly one endpoint is the depot (depot↔node trunk legs) and 35 km/h otherwise (inter-node), plus add 120 s service time at every customer visit when computing route duration; use this function uniformly in construction, delta evaluation, and final cost.
extension_recipes.workload_balance: Add a balance penalty to the objective: total_time + λ * (max_route_duration - min_route_duration), or constrain each route's duration within [mean*(1-α), mean*(1+α)]; during K-means, weight points by demand and target equal cluster sums; include a cross-route relocate/swap operator that only accepts moves which reduce the max route duration.
extension_recipes.spatial_compactness: Use K-means (or capacitated K-means) on (lon,lat) so clusters are convex; when rebalancing for capacity, always move a boundary customer to its geographically nearest feasible cluster; after routing, run a cross-route 2-opt* only between geographically adjacent clusters to avoid creating crossings.
extension_recipes.single_class_per_vehicle_segregation: Before any routing: partition customers by hazmat_class into disjoint pools and route each pool independently with its own subset of vehicles. In feasibility check enforce two separate predicates: (1) len({p.hazmat_class for p in route})==1, (2) that class ∈ vehicle.allowed_classes. Never merge classes even if a vehicle is certified for several.
extension_recipes.edge_level_road_restrictions: Load ALL restriction types from the data (do not hardcode keywords); build FORBIDDEN[hazmat_class] as a set of frozenset({u,v}) (undirected); apply INF masking uniformly to every cost/risk/time matrix used by any Dijkstra or local-search call, per class; check forbidden edges inside every move operator (greedy insert, 2-opt, Or-opt, relocate, swap) before accepting; expand Dijkstra hop-by-hop and re-validate the full expanded path; never emit 'flag as violation' fallbacks—if no feasible path, split the route or drop to a longer detour.
extension_recipes.max_route_duration: Track cumulative route duration (drive time + service time + rest time) and reject any insertion/move whose new duration exceeds 10 h; during construction, close the route and start a new one (or reject the customer for this vehicle) when the next insertion would breach the limit.
extension_recipes.mandatory_driver_rest: Maintain a running odometer per route; whenever cumulative driven distance since the last rest crosses a 160 km boundary, add 30 min rest to the route duration before the next leg; include this rest cost in delta evaluation so local-search moves see the true post-rest duration, and re-check the 10 h cap after every move.
